metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth sit in the same uptime category as backup power, because a degraded fabric burns GPU-hours before it becomes an outage.

The category groups three measurements: UPS battery health and generator runtime, SLA uptime compliance, and the network itself. Two of those are about keeping electricity flowing. The third treats the internal fabric and external transit as a continuously measured resource, tracking round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization rather than waiting for a link to fail outright.

That placement matters for AI specifically. The stated reason is that distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation, and that a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage. This is a different failure mode from a power cut. A cut is visible and immediate. Degradation is quiet, and the cost accumulates in compute that was paid for and did not produce useful work.

What the data does not supply is any threshold, target, or measured value. It names what to measure and why, not what counts as acceptable, and it gives no history and no facility count. A reader learns that fabric health is classified as an uptime concern, not how healthy any particular fabric is.
